events.title: Demo Update 0.9.6: Clearer at a Glance
events.summary: "Oh. You found the one I hid. Fine. Take it." — The Tower A small update built from two playtests, mostly about one thing: seeing what just happened. ON SCREEN Notifications no longer cover your knight. Announcements are a small card in a corner of the screen (your half in co-op), and the game's cues sit under the top bar. events.title: Demo Update 0.9.5: New Card Screens, Fair Warnings, Meaner Wardens
events.summary: "CHAOS terms accepted. No refunds. I am going to enjoy this." — The Tower Everything since 0.9.4 in one update. The three big ones first: new card screens, a game that tells you the move the moment you need it, and Wardens that hit as hard as the difficulty you picked. NEW CARD SCREENS Level-up, the ult pick, the free reward and the market now use new stone-tablet screens. Every card on a screen uses the same text size. events.title: Demo Update 0.9.4: The Tower Redecorated
events.summary: "I redecorated. Leave the bodies where they fall. They're part of the look." — The Tower Everything since 0.9.1 in one update: a new look for the whole tower, a real door with a stair behind it, an opening cinematic, and a long list of control fixes. A NEW LOOK The tower has been relit from the first floor up. Light travels with you, and the edges of the room fall into real dark. events.title: Demo Update 0.9.1: The Tower Grew a Body
events.summary: "You came back. Good. I was getting hungry." — The Tower The TOWERMOUTH demo has been rebuilt from the inside. Here is what changed. STACK THRESHOLDS Five effect cards now have a threshold. Collect five copies of the same effect and it changes shape: Lightning Rod, Fuse Fist, Blood Web, Thorn Garden or Echo. events.title: THANK YOU GUYS
events.summary: Over 1,000 people have added the TOWERMOUTH demo to their Steam library. For a game nobody had heard of, made by one person, that took a while to believe.The wishlist side is smaller and slower. TOWERMOUTH is at 93 right now — seven away from its first hundred. Small numbers, but they are real people, and I can see every one of them.I build all of it: the tower, the monsters, the loot, the weapons, the two-player couch mode.
